E9-1-service-reconciler.reason: E9's exit gate opens with `desired state` and `placement`; SVC-002 is the control-plane half. TIMING: SVC-002-design.md 9.2 predicted this clause would land `unwired`, on the GO-BOOK's 2026-08-28 ruling that an E9 clause was PREMATURE `no real service-execution symbol to track until SVC-002 lands ... so a clause would be vacuous`. That ruling named its own release condition and it is now met: SVC-002 lands the symbol AND its arming path in one commit. PRODUCTION CALLERS: 0 at base (the symbol did not exist), 2 at head as the guard's own `countProductionCallers` measures it -- and those two lines are ONE composition site in server/src/index.ts, the dynamic-import binding plus the call, inside the `config.distributedExecutionEnabled && distributedExecutionDatabases` block. The measured figure is stated rather than the intuitive one because the guard counts the `const { createServiceReconciler } = await import(...)` line too (its import-stripping regex only blanks static `import ... from` forms). That block builds the reconciler, drives it on a `nextDelayMs` backoff timer, and stops it on SIGTERM/SIGINT. Registered inside that block for MIG-002's measured reason, not by copying it: flag-off allocates no `aoa_app` pool, so `runInTenant` would have nothing to open and unconditional registration would be a throw rather than a safety net. WHAT THE CLAUSE CLAIMS, NARROWLY: when a `services` row exists with `desired_state='running'` and a `service_generations` definition for its generation, the reconciler creates EXACTLY ONE `service_instances` row and EXACTLY ONE `service` job for it, in one transaction, and never a second -- idempotently across ticks, across concurrent passes, and across a writer that takes no lock at all. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM, and each of these is the difference between this clause and the epic's gate: (1) NOTHING CREATES A SERVICE. `services` has one insert in the tree with ZERO production callers and SVC-002 adds no route (SVC-007 owns create/update/pause/resume/stop), so on a real deployment the tick reads an empty window and converges nothing -- E9's exit gate is NOT met by this ticket and this ticket does not claim it is. (2) `service_generations` likewise has ZERO writers, so even a hand-inserted service stalls at `{action:'none', reason:'no_generation'}` rather than starting with an invented command; the unreadable-intent branch is a deliberate stall, not a default. (3) It converges zero instances to one and then goes quiescent: `recordServiceHealth` is the only writer of `service_instances.status` and has no consumer, so nothing here drives an instance terminal (SVC-003). (4) `drain` means a draining target is not SELECTED for a new instance; moving or stopping an instance already running on a draining target is SVC-003/SVC-005. (5) A submitted service job is placed `queued`/`no_eligible_target` unless a daemon advertises `workload.service` with a free service slot, and E9-F002 stays open. E9-2-service-supervisor.reason: E9's exit gate names supervision of a service instance; SVC-008b is the daemon half (SVC-008-design.md §11.2). WIRED, and enrolled as `wired` rather than the `unwired` the design predicted, because the design wrote that line when the constant widening was still hypothetical: SVC-008b actually dispatches to the symbol. PRODUCTION CALLERS: ONE, as the guard measures it — the `handoff.offer.job.workloadType === "service"` branch in `runLifecycle` (packages/worker-daemon/src/supervisor/supervisor.ts), which sits on the shipped lease path `createSupervisor` -> `accept` -> `runLifecycle`, and `createSupervisor` is composed in production by `lifecycle/dispatch-runtime.ts`. WHAT THE CLAUSE CLAIMS, NARROWLY: a service job reaches a worker and is SUPERVISED AS A SERVICE — launched via `startProcess` (an acknowledgement, not a completion), health-ticked from `processStatus`, stopped through a cancel->kill ladder whose verdict comes from an observation, and terminalized with the frozen service-instance events. It does NOT claim services are MANAGED: health semantics + the `service_health` -> `recordServiceHealth` projection are SVC-003's, restart/checkpoint are SVC-004's, drain/generation are SVC-005's, and there is still no human path to create a service (SVC-007). SVC-008b adds NO consumer of `recordServiceHealth` and no `service_health` state projection: the symbol's reference set is UNCHANGED by this diff, base to head, as the register's own counter reports. (The reason line previously said `recordServiceHealth` "keeps its zero production callers"; that number was wrong — the counter reports the same non-zero figure at base and at head. The substance, no new consumer, is what the clause needs and is what is asserted here.) PROVEN, NOT DECLARED: packages/worker-daemon/src/__tests__/svc-008b-service-supervisor.test.ts (T1-T7 + a NAMED positive control) was observed 12-red / 2-green against the unchanged tree, and six mutants were killed — deleting the dispatch (12 red), synthesizing `healthy` on an unwitnessed read, deriving the stop verdict from `ProcessSignalResult.accepted` instead of its observation, dropping the per-tick fence check, dropping the capability-freshness stop, and killing before the graceful rung. The positive control stayed green under every one. server/src/__tests__/u0-d1-placement-reachability.test.ts carries T0: the committed worker-b ceiling now leaves the shipped daemon's DERIVED hello offerable a real service job through the real `evaluateStaticLeaseEligibility`; reverting the constant reds T0 and the exact-equality pin while both batch cases stay green. RESIDUAL, ON THE RECORD: a service run is bounded at RUN_OP_DEADLINE_CEILING_MS (240 s) because the owned-labels capability is minted on one route with a 5-minute TTL and never re-minted; the loop stops on the teardown headroom rather than orphan a billable sandbox. Whether a four-minute service is worth advertising is SVC-008 §9.1 and is UNRULED.

PRODUCTION CALLERS, measured with this guard's own `countProductionCallers`, base `6b39c77f6` vs head: `applyServiceProjectionForFence` 0 -> 1 (the per-event branch inside `acceptEvent`, itself on the shipped JOB-005 ingest path `workerControlRoutes` -> `createJobEventIngestService.ingest` -> `repos.jobControl.acceptEvent`); `writeServiceInstanceStatus` 0 -> 2 (the projection and `recordServiceHealth`, which now share the ONE writer of that column so the two cannot drift); `decideServiceProjectionForEvent` 0 -> 1; `predecessorsOf` 0 -> 1; and `canTransitionServiceInstanceStatus` 0 -> 1, which is the point of that last line: the FROZEN `SERVICE_INSTANCE_TRANSITIONS` table had ZERO production consumers at base, so the lifecycle it defines was a clause nothing enforced. `recordServiceHealth` is 2 at base and 2 at head -- unchanged, because the projection does not call it; both are entry points onto the shared writer. `createStartupReconciler`, the cautionary zero-caller neighbour, is untouched at 0. WHAT THE CLAUSE CLAIMS, NARROWLY: an accepted worker event that WITNESSES an instance fact moves `service_instances.status` inside the same fenced transaction that appends it, idempotently on a `service_instance_status` projection receipt, and every other event moves nothing. The authority for WHICH row is `service_instances.job_id`/`.attempt_id` (SVC-002's attribution), never the worker-controlled `payload.serviceInstanceId` -- which is unauthorized by construction (E9-F003), so a mismatched claim is REFUSED. The generation on the instance row is the FENCE SVC-002 scoped out by name, and a stale-generation event is refused. Legality is the frozen transition table, so no event can move an instance OUT of `stopped`/`failed`/`lost`: that is the DE-12 split-brain refusal, because a terminal instance has left `service_instances_live_service_uq` and SVC-002 has already replaced it. An attempt with no attributed instance answers `unattributed` -- an explicit unknown that writes nothing, never a default status. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM, and each is the difference between this clause and E9's gate: (1) NOTHING CREATES A SERVICE -- `services` still has one insert with zero production callers and no route (SVC-007), so on a real deployment there is no instance for this projection to move; E9's exit gate is NOT met and this ticket does not claim it is. (2) The rest of SVC-003's Outcome is NOT delivered: no liveness deadline (a worker that goes silent without emitting anything is still only reaped at the LEASE level, and nothing terminalizes its instance), no graceful-stop or checkpoint request path, and no bounded lease-renewal change. SVC-003 stays OPEN. (3) Memory/context callbacks and connector refresh under the current fence are NOT built and are not buildable yet -- `MemoryActor` has no `service` kind and no memory op exists among the ten frozen worker operations (SVC-001-design.md section 4). (4) No partition test: no replica identity or partition detector exists anywhere in the tree. PROVEN, NOT DECLARED: server/src/__tests__/service-health-projection.integration.test.ts (11 cases over real embedded PostgreSQL and a real poll/ACK-minted ACTIVE fence, T1 driving the FULL `createJobEventIngestService` path so the decider is proven reachable from the wire -- and T1 is the ONLY case that drives that ingest, so the production wire is proven by exactly ONE arm: the `serviceProjection: null` mutant below reds T1 and nothing else, which is both the arming discrimination and the thinness) and server/src/__tests__/service-health-projection.test.ts (15 pure cases over the whole 9x9 transition table). The kills: delete the `attempt_started` -> `leased` arm (10 red -- without it `pending` is a dead end and the whole projection is production-unreachable), map `service_instance_started` to `healthy` (5), return the transition table unfiltered (7), project `stopping` from `service_graceful_stop_observed` (1), default an unreadable health verdict to `healthy` (2), REINSTATE `"interrupted"` in the health-status domain (2 -- this is the genuine BASE-TREE state, E9-F001), delete the legality check (1 -- T5, the split-brain case), trust `payload.serviceInstanceId` (1 -- T4), delete the generation fence (1 -- T3), return a definite `applied` for an unattributed observation (1 -- T7), have the projection bump `leases.expires_at` (1 -- T6, E9's "health events do not extend ownership" clause), delete the call site in `acceptEvent` (10 red, positive control still green), set `serviceProjection: null` in the ingest's `toAcceptInputs` (1 -- and ONLY T1, which is exactly the arming discrimination: the feature wired to nothing while every other case passes), and the four added by the review fixes -- revert `predecessorsOf` to the direct-edge filter (3), delete the attempt-terminal backstop (3), default `whenAlreadyTerminal` to `"noop"` (2, one of them T5 itself), and walk back through PROJECTABLE states too (3). ★★★ TWO REAL DEFECTS IN THIS DIFF WERE FOUND BY EXTERNAL REVIEW, NOT BY THE SUITE, AND BOTH WERE PERMANENT WEDGES -- recorded here because the shape of the miss is the point. (i) E9-F004: `SERVICE_INSTANCE_TRANSITIONS` makes `stopping` the SOLE predecessor of `stopped` and NO frozen worker event can assert `stopping` (the supervisor emits `service_instance_stopped` directly from `healthy` at `runServiceLifecycle`'s `case "process_exited"` arm at service-lifecycle.ts ~:293, and `gracefulStop`'s `verdict === "stopped"` branch at ~:362), so the first revision's direct-edge legality predicate refused EVERY NORMAL SERVICE STOP as `illegal_transition`, leaving the instance inside `service_instances_live_service_uq` where the reconciler could never replace it. It survived a named positive control and thirteen killed mutants because the only end-to-end case drove `service_instance_lost`, which the frozen table makes reachable from every non-terminal status -- a lifecycle table proven over the transitions a suite happens to exercise is not proven over the table. Fixed by admitting paths whose every INTERMEDIATE step is a status no event can project; the residual (`stopped` now admitted from `leased` too) is FILED as E9-F004 and stays open. (ii) E9-F005: a launch resolving no handle emits no `service_instance_started` (`runServiceLifecycle`'s §4.2a launch comment at service-lifecycle.ts ~:166 says so in terms), so a failed attempt left the instance `leased` forever; fixed with the attempt-terminal backstop and filed as E9-F005, resolved here.

E9-4-service-liveness-deadline.reason: E9's exit gate names `health` AND `restart`; SVC-003a wired the first half and this is the piece between them: the deadline that notices an instance is no longer live WHEN NOTHING SAID SO. WHAT WAS TRUE BEFORE: every path SVC-003a built is edge-triggered by an accepted worker event, and SVC-003a's own result says the gap in terms -- "a worker that goes silent WITHOUT EMITTING ANYTHING is still only reaped at the LEASE level, and nothing terminalizes its instance". Measured at head before this ticket: `reapExpiredLeases` revokes the lease and terminalizes the ATTEMPT and the JOB and contains no write to `service_instances` at all, so the instance stayed inside `service_instances_live_service_uq` and SVC-002's reconciler could never replace it. That is the case L-T8 measures rather than asserts. The dangerous variant is worse: `lease-renewal.ts` renews on a driver separate from the supervise loop, and `runServiceLifecycle`'s health step handles an unanswerable `processStatus` read with `unknown => EMIT NOTHING` (its own comment closes "SVC-003 owns the liveness DEADLINE policy"), so a worker whose supervision has gone silent while renewal continues holds a lease that never expires and is invisible to the reaper entirely. PRODUCTION CALLERS, measured with this guard's own `countProductionCallers`, base `053f90fc8` vs head: `sweepOrganizationServiceLiveness` 0 -> 1 (the pass inside `createServiceReconciler`'s own `runTick`, ahead of the convergence pages); `sweepServiceInstanceLiveness` 0 -> 3, of which only ONE is a call -- the guard also counts the repository interface declaration and its implementation, the same reason SVC-003a records 2 for `recordServiceHealth`; `classifyServiceInstanceLiveness` 0 -> 1; `livenessVerdictTerminalizes` 0 -> 1; `livenessDeadlineAllowedFromStatuses` 0 -> 2 (the sweep and the module's own load-time coverage assertion); `SERVICE_LIVENESS_DEADLINE_TO_STATUS` 0 -> 3; `writeServiceInstanceStatus` 2 -> 3 at this ticket's head and 4 at the MERGED head (the deadline is the THIRD entry point onto the one writer of that column, and SVC-007a's `terminalizeServiceInstanceForCancelledAttempt` -- merged in afterwards -- is the FOURTH; four entry points, still one writer and one idea of a legal move); `predecessorsOf` 1 -> 2. UNCHANGED and re-measured rather than recited: `applyServiceProjectionForFence` 1 -> 1, `createServiceReconciler` 2 -> 2, `recordServiceHealth` 2 -> 2, `reapExpiredLeases` 3 -> 3, and the cautionary neighbour `createStartupReconciler` 0 -> 0. WHAT THE CLAUSE CLAIMS, NARROWLY: a live `service_instances` row whose worker has stopped being observed is driven to the frozen `lost` status by a clock rather than by an event, it leaves `service_instances_live_service_uq`, and SVC-002's unchanged reconciler creates its replacement -- in the SAME tick, because the sweep runs ahead of the convergence pages. TWO WINDOWS, AND THEY NEVER SUBSTITUTE: an instance that HAS been observed is aged against a short liveness window; one that has NEVER been observed has no liveness fact to age and is aged against `created_at` under a separate, longer admission window. Collapsing them in either direction is a defect with a name and both are mutation-pinned (L4/L15 for the short-window collapse, L5 for the infinitely-stale collapse). WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM, and each is the difference between this clause and the epic's gate: (1) NOTHING STILL CREATES A SERVICE -- `repos.services.insert` has the same ZERO production callers it had at base and this ticket adds no route (SVC-007), so on a real deployment the sweep reads an empty population and terminalizes nothing. (2) `service_generations` still has no writer, so a replacement stalls at `no_generation` on a real deployment exactly as SVC-002 records. (3) The deadline terminalizes the INSTANCE and does NOT fence the WORKER: it writes exactly one table (L-T11, mutant L17), so a silent-but-still-renewing worker keeps its lease while its replacement starts. The replacement is protected by SVC-003a's split-brain refusal; the old worker's external effects are not, and that residual is filed as E9-F007 and belongs to SVC-005's overlap clause. (4) WHETHER a terminalized instance should be replaced at all, and with what backoff, is SVC-004's crash-loop clause and this ticket has no opinion about it. PROVEN, NOT DECLARED: server/src/__tests__/service-liveness-deadline.test.ts (15 pure cases) and server/src/__tests__/service-liveness-deadline.integration.test.ts (13 cases, real embedded PostgreSQL, real poll/ACK-minted ACTIVE fence, the real shipped reaper). TWENTY mutants were applied to the shipped source by a harness that refuses to apply over an existing backup, tries BOTH line-ending forms of every anchor and THROWS on a miss, rebuilds `dist` for repository mutants, and byte-verifies each restore; a green unmutated baseline was measured before and after the campaign. Every one killed at least one case and the NAMED POSITIVE CONTROL (`L-T9 POSITIVE CONTROL -- SVC-002's convergence is untouched by the deadline`) stayed green under nineteen of the twenty. L7 is the exception and is a NON-RUN rather than a survival: it makes the module throw at load, so neither suite collects and no case executes, the control included -- said this way because a control that did not run is not a control that held. ★ ONE MUTANT SURVIVED THE FIRST CAMPAIGN AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DROPPED: L14 (delete the sweep's independent legality gate) killed NOTHING, because `lost` is legal from all six live statuses so the gate is unreachable through the shipped caller. The gate was kept and pinned by a case that performs the narrow call itself (L-T10), the same shape SVC-002's T1c uses for its own unreachable property. ★★★ AND EXTERNAL REVIEW OF PR #413 FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN THIS DIFF, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE OF WHAT IT WAS: the sweep read `ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT n`, and a HEALTHY instance never leaves the live set -- so for a tenant with more live instances than one batch holds, the oldest-created healthy rows filled the batch on every tick and a silent instance created after them was NEVER INSPECTED. That is a stuck service the deadline itself cannot see, i.e. the exact failure this clause claims to remove, and it is the SAME starvation bug review caught in `listReconcilableServices` on PR #406 -- whose correction note sits a few hundred lines above the new query in the same file. Fixed by ordering on `COALESCE(last_observed_at, created_at)` (an ORDERING, not a verdict: mutant L15 pins that collapsing the two instants in the SELECT is still a defect), pinned by L-T12, and mutant L18 restores the defect. Two smaller review points landed with it: a terminalizing tick no longer backs off to the idle delay (L19), and each condemned instance is now reported individually (L20) -- the DURABLE half of that record is deliberately NOT built and is filed as E9-F009.

E9-4-service-create-and-desired-state.reason: E9's exit gate opens with `desired state` and `generation`, and until this clause nothing on a real deployment could produce either. THE STATE AT BASE, in the words of three shipped documents that all said it and were all right: SVC-002-result.md section 7 ("Nothing creates a service. `repos.services.insert` keeps its zero production callers and SVC-002 adds no routes. The reconciler reconciles rows only a test can create ... Nothing writes a generation."), SVC-003a-result.md section 2 ("NOTHING CREATES A SERVICE ... so on a real deployment there is no `services` row, so no instance, so nothing for this projection to move"), and E9-1's own reason above, which lists both as things it does NOT claim. SVC-002's reconciler and SVC-003a's projection were therefore SHIPPED AND UNREACHABLE. PRODUCTION CALLERS, measured with this guard's own `countProductionCallers`, base `053f90fc8` vs head: `createServiceWithinTenant` 0 -> 1 (`createService`, which the POST route calls); `createService`/`setServiceDesiredState`/`setServiceDesiredStateWithinTenant`/`readService`/`listServices`/`normalizeServiceDefinition` 0 -> 1 each (the four routes in `jobControlRoutes`); `insertServiceGeneration`, `updateServiceDesiredState`, `terminalizeServiceInstanceForCancelledAttempt`, `findServiceForCompany` and `listServicesForCompany` 0 -> 3 each and `findLiveServiceInstance` 0 -> 4 -- the MEASURED figures are stated rather than the intuitive ones, because for a tenant-repository method the guard counts the interface declaration and the implementation alongside the call site; `canTransitionServiceDesiredState` 0 -> 1, which is the second dead frozen fence this epic has armed (its table had ZERO production consumers, exactly as `canTransitionServiceInstanceStatus` did before SVC-003a); `lockServiceForReconcile` 3 -> 4 (the desired-state control REUSES SVC-002's per-service advisory lock rather than minting a second key -- two locks are one lock fewer); `decideServiceProjection` 1 -> 2. `repos.services.insert`, which is a property access the counter cannot see, has ZERO production call sites at base and ONE at head (`createServiceWithinTenant`), measured by grep over non-test sources. `createStartupReconciler`, the cautionary zero-caller neighbour, is untouched at 0; `createServiceReconciler` is 2 at base and 2 at head. THE COMPOSITION ROOT IS `jobControlRoutes` in `server/src/routes/job-control.ts`, mounted by `createApp` (`server/src/app.ts`) inside the `opts.distributedExecutionEnabled` block over the non-owner `aoa_app` pool -- the same router that carries JOB-008's operator surface, using the SAME `execution_target:manage` org-admin gate (`assertOrgAdmin`) run FIRST on every route -- literally first, since these four routes carry NO `validate(...)` middleware and parse their body schema INSIDE the handler after the gate. That is the fix for a P2 external review raised: `validate` is middleware, so it ran BEFORE the handler and therefore before the gate, answering an unauthorized caller with a 400 about their body while the same caller with a well-shaped body got the 403. A thrown ZodError reaches the same error handler `validate` relied on, so only the ORDER moves.
